topomer.note: only 3 of 29 molecules can be cut at the framework

descriptors.note: 10 descriptors; dropped as the activity under another name: mwila_pooled_raw; not usable as a baseline (see the warning)

findings.text: 22 chemotype(s); the largest holds 3 of 29 molecules -- a series of several scaffolds has no common frame, and an alignment will invent one
the common framework (framework of the largest chemotype) has 20 heavy atoms, about 118% of a typical molecule, and 10% of the set can be cut at it
the 20 shared framework atoms sit 1.3 A apart between molecules, over the best of their matches (3 of 29 carry them) -- the molecules are not in a common frame

the descriptor baseline reproduces the activity almost exactly (q2 +0.992); on a set this size that is not chemistry but the measurement itself, reached through the file's own columns -- the nearest are mwila_hcl_adj (r 0.93), mwila_pooled_adj (r 0.92), db_id (r 0.27), n_papers (r 0.23). No descriptor conclusion can be drawn until they are excluded.
dropped from the descriptor baseline because they reproduce the activity rather than describe the molecule: mwila_pooled_raw -- if one of these is a real descriptor, name it and run again
the aligned model is +0.139 in q2 against counts (95% interval -0.309 to +0.475) -- the frame buys nothing over counts
the aligned model is +0.103 in q2 against invariant (95% interval -0.287 to +0.459) -- the frame buys nothing over invariant
the aligned model is -1.081 in q2 against descriptors (95% interval -1.559 to -0.900) -- descriptors alone do as well, so the geometry is decoration on this set

why: no route reaches q2 0.1 (best aligned at -0.089); the set does not support a model as it stands
